content: A system of morality which is based on relative emotional values is a mere illusion, a vulgar conception which has nothing sound in it.
author: Socrates
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Living in pretense takes an enormous amount of mental energy. When you constantly manage impressions to please others, you end up feeling like an imposter in your own skin.

In Socrates's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Honesty with yourself can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is the only ground upon which a real life can be built. When you stop lying to yourself about your feelings, your energy is immediately freed up.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
